test_title: PYST 13: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which fort is an example of Rajput military architecture?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chittorgarh Fort**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chittorgarh Fort** is widely considered one of the most outstanding examples of **Rajput military architecture**. It is located in the **Chittorgarh** district of **Rajasthan**, India, and stands as a symbol of Rajput bravery and resistance.
 
• Spanning over an area of approximately **700 acres** and situated on a **180-meter high hill**, it is one of the largest forts in India. It served as the capital of the **Mewar Kingdom** for centuries.
 
• In **2013**, it was designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** under the "Hill Forts of Rajasthan" group, highlighting its **historical significance** and structural brilliance.
 
• The fort features seven massive gates (called **Pols**), such as the **Padan Pol** and **Bhairon Pol**, designed to hinder enemy advancement. It also contains iconic structures like the **Vijay Stambh** (Tower of Victory), built by **Rana Kumbha** in **1448** to commemorate his victory over the armies of Malwa and Gujarat.
 
• The architecture showcases the use of **natural topography** for defense, a hallmark of **Rajput** engineering, which prioritized high elevation and massive stone **ramparts** to withstand long sieges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Red Fort (Delhi)**: This fort is a prime example of **Mughal architecture**. It was commissioned by Emperor **Shah Jahan** in **1639** and completed in **1648**. Its **features** include massive walls of **red sandstone** and a layout that represents the zenith of Mughal creativity, blending Persian, Timurid, and Indian styles.
 
• **Agra Fort**: Located in **Agra**, **Uttar Pradesh**, this fort is another **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. While it has ancient origins as a brick fort called **Badalgarh**, it was rebuilt in its current form by Mughal Emperor **Akbar** starting in **1565**. It served as the main residence of the Mughal dynasty until **1638**.
 
• **Golkonda Fort**: Situated in **Hyderabad**, **Telangana**, it was the capital of the **Qutb Shahi dynasty** (**1512–1687**). It is famous for its **acoustic features**; a handclap at the entrance can be heard at the **Bala Hissar** pavilion, which is the highest point of the fort. It was also once the center of the global **diamond trade**.
 
• **Rajput vs. Mughal Styles**: While **Mughal architecture** often focused on symmetry, **charbagh gardens**, and marble inlay (pietra dura), **Rajput military architecture** was characterized by ruggedness, **jharokhas** (overhanging balconies), **chhatris** (cenotaphs), and defensive **bastions** tailored to the desert or hilly terrain of **Rajasthan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Chittorgarh Fort** is immortalized in history due to the three **Jauhars** (mass self-immolation) performed by the women of the fort during defeats, most notably the one led by **Rani Padmini** in **1303** when **Alauddin Khalji** attacked.
 
• The fort's **water management system** was highly advanced for its time, consisting of **84 water bodies** (reservoirs, wells, and step-wells) that could store enough water to sustain an army of **50,000 soldiers** for four years without external supply.
 
• **Kirti Stambh**, another major landmark within the fort, is a **22-meter high** tower dedicated to the first Jain Tirthankara, **Rishabhanatha**, highlighting the **religious diversity** present in Rajput kingdoms during the **12th century**.
 
• The battle of **Haldighati** (**1576**) and the subsequent struggles of **Maharana Pratap** are closely linked to the legacy of the **Mewar** resistance centered around this architectural marvel.
